record.context_brief: Polynomial-size families with perfect state transfer
record.original_question: Find an infinite family of graphs that admit perfect state transfer and whose size grows only polynomially with the diameter. Here perfect state transfer means that for some time t and some vertices u and v, the continuous-time quantum walk transition matrix U(t) = exp(itA) maps the characteristic vector of u to a unit-modulus scalar multiple of the characteristic vector of v.

evidence.quote: It is plausible that there is a subfamily of Cartesian powers of P2 for which this compressing procedure can be described in such a way that the resulting graphs are bounded by a polynomial in the diameter.
2.2 Open Problem. Find an infinite family of graphs for which there is perfect state transfer, and the size of the graph is bounded by a polynomial in the diameter.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph with adjacency matrix $A$. The continuous-time quantum walk on $G$ is defined by the unitary transition matrix $U(t) = \exp(itA)$ for $t \in \mathbb{R}$. For two distinct vertices $u, v \in V$, with characteristic (standard basis) vectors $e_u, e_v \in \mathbb{C}^{V}$, we say that $G$ admits perfect state transfer from $u$ to $v$ if there exist $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\gamma \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|\gamma| = 1$ such that
$$U(t)\, e_u = \gamma\, e_v.$$
The diameter $\mathrm{diam}(G)$ is the largest graph distance between any two vertices of $G$, and the size $|G|$ is the number of vertices.

Construct an infinite family $\{G_n\}_{n\ge 1}$ of finite simple graphs, with $\mathrm{diam}(G_n) \to \infty$, such that:
(i) each $G_n$ admits perfect state transfer between some pair of its vertices, and
(ii) there exists a polynomial $p$ with $|G_n| \le p(\mathrm{diam}(G_n))$ for all $n$.

Equivalently, exhibit an infinite family of graphs admitting perfect state transfer whose number of vertices is bounded by a polynomial in the diameter.
artifact.category_tag: quantum walks and perfect state transfer
artifact.status_search_result: Known infinite families with perfect state transfer (paths P2, P3; their Cartesian powers; certain circulant graphs; cubelike graphs; some distance-regular graphs of small diameter) are either of fixed small diameter or have size growing exponentially in the diameter (e.g., Cartesian powers of P2 give 2^n vertices but diameter n). Recent works construct families with peak/pretty good state transfer of polynomial size in the distance, but no construction of an infinite polynomial-size family achieving exact perfect state transfer is reported. The problem appears to remain open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Peak state transfer in continuous quantum walks
status_evidence.snippet: a family of graphs which achieves peak state transfer at arbitrarily long distances while keeping the size of the graphs bounded by a polynomial on the distance
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-size families are known for peak (approximate) state transfer, but the perfect state transfer analogue is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: An Infinite Family of Circulant Graphs with Perfect State Transfer
status_evidence.snippet: infinite family of 4-regular circulant graphs that admit perfect state transfer
status_evidence.claim: Existing infinite families of graphs with perfect state transfer do not satisfy the polynomial-in-diameter size bound.

status_evidence.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on association schemes and distance-regular graphs
status_evidence.snippet: characterized perfect state transfer on distance-regular graphs of diameter 2 and 3
status_evidence.claim: Recent results focus on small fixed diameter, leaving the polynomial-size question for unbounded diameter open.
